turns.q:
Your response was: "Looked at it. Checkout flow. Nearly missed the submit button. It barely registered visually — took a moment to find the action I needed."

We want to understand what you meant by "nearly missed the submit button", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The “Place Order” button is positioned below the much more prominent “Continue Shopping” button, making the final checkout action feel visually secondary.  
B) The “Place Order” button appears low in the layout, beneath the payment form and legal text area, so it feels buried rather than part of the main checkout hierarchy.  
C) The button label “Place Order” is present, but the surrounding layout does not clearly mark it as the primary submission action for the checkout flow.  
D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.

What specifically around the “Place Order” button—its placement below “Continue Shopping,” its lighter styling, or the nearby legal text—makes it seem less clearly marked as the checkout submission action?
turns.a: Lighter one disappeared into the background. Almost looked inactive.

turns.q: If this layout were built exactly as shown, would the pale “Place Order” treatment mainly make the final checkout action harder to notice, or would it suggest the action is unavailable?
turns.a: 'Place Order.' Faint. Label barely there. Easy to overlook — didn't register where it should.

turns.q: Does the faint “Place Order” area make the main checkout submission harder to locate in this layout, or harder to recognize as the action once noticed?
turns.a: 'Continue Shopping' pulled the eye — looked like the action. 'Place Order' had nothing pulling toward it. Nearly treated the wrong one as the submit step. Re-read before moving.

turns.q: When the faint “Place Order” area disappears beside the darker “Continue Shopping” button, what does that tell you this bottom action area is structurally getting wrong?
turns.a: More visible. Bigger. Has to stand out — can't be the one you scan past.

turns.q: If the design team could change only one structural thing in this bottom action area, what would make “Place Order” clearly read as the checkout submission instead of the button you scan past?
turns.a: Solid fill: brand color — dark blue, green, anything with sufficient contrast against white. White label text at 14–16px minimum. Standard primary button treatment. Distinction from 'Continue Shopping' needs to be legible: primary CTA gets the fill, secondary gets the outline or text link. Right now 'Place Order' is invisible and 'Continue Shopping' is visible. They're backwards. One CSS change to background-color, color, and font-size. Done.
